title: Playing the Clark Street honky tonks with Herb Morand
summary: In Chicago he played with Herb Morand in three-piece combos at the Firehouse and Lawrence O'Brien's joint on Clark Street.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: And here in Chicago, your place was Hurt Moran. Oh, Hurt Moran.
And where did you play with Hurt Moran?
On Clock Street in the Honky Tonks. The Firehouse. The joint they call the Firehouse. And Lawrence O'Brien, the Irishman. Where? Lawrence O'Brien's joint.
On Clock Street. That was nothing but Honky Tonks and off Clock Street. Nothing but Honky Tonks. Yeah. All one after another.
Just Hurt Moran and you or somebody else? Oh, no.
We had three pieces. Didn't use none of the three piece combo in them. Just piano drums or saxophone drums. Three piece of combo. That's all they used.
